title: Reaper Convergence Report
markdown:
# Convergence Report — Unanswered-Message Reaper

## ELI16 Overview

When you send a message in Telegram and your agent goes quiet — no response, no error, just silence — that's a **silent dead-drop**. We saw two flavors of it on the Luna/SageMind agent: (1) a message arrives during a context-compaction window and the agent never processes it, and (2) the agent DOES process the message and writes a great answer in its terminal, but never relays that answer back to Telegram.

The fix is a small new piece called the **Unanswered-Message Reaper**. It runs in the background every 60 seconds and asks one question, per topic: "is the user waiting on a reply that's more than 3 minutes old?" If yes, it nudges the agent to respond — and if the agent already did respond but it never made it to Telegram, the nudge specifically tells the agent to relay it now (with safety rails so the agent doesn't blindly forward internal diagnostics or cross-topic content).

Originally I planned this as a simple periodic loop. Reviews from seven angles (security, scalability, edge-case attacks, integration, plus three external AI models) caught a lot. The shipped design is now much more careful: it knows the difference between an agent that's actually thinking versus one that's stuck, it can't be tricked by hostile message content, it doesn't accidentally double-fire when two machines are both syncing the same state, it survives a server restart without losing track of what it's already done, and it caps the worst-case user-visible silence at 10 minutes via a "your agent appears stuck" notification on the dashboard.

## Original vs Converged

**Originally**: A 60-second loop that scanned every topic, found the last user message with no agent reply, and re-injected a recovery prompt. Two prompt modes (silent vs diverged). Persisted dedupe to avoid spamming. Done.

**After review**: same shape, with the following new structural pieces:

- **Channel discriminator on every entry.** Originally entries were just `(topicId, sessionName)`. Reviewers noticed Telegram and Slack could collide on identifier shape — same topicId could route a Slack message into a Telegram session. Now every entry carries `channel: 'telegram' | 'slack'`, and dedupe keys are channel-qualified so collisions are impossible.

- **Time semantics split.** Originally one ambiguous "timestamp." Reviewers caught that comparing a process-local monotonic clock against file-system mtimes and persisted timestamps is silently broken across restarts. Now there are two explicit fields — wall-clock for persistence and comparison, monotonic for in-process elapsed checks only — and every comparison names the field it uses.

- **Mode B classification is now four gates, not two.** Originally Mode B (the "agent answered in terminal but didn't relay" path) fired whenever the JSONL had grown after the user's message and was idle for 30 seconds. Three separate reviewers caught that a slow LLM API call or a `npm test` looks identical to "agent finished" under that rule. Now Mode B requires: mtime grew, JSONL idle 90 seconds (not 30), no active child processes (with try/catch — failures count as "still working"), AND a positive at-prompt signal from SessionWatchdog. Fail any gate → fall back to the safer Mode A prompt.

- **Mode B prompt no longer says "re-send your last response."** Reviewers caught that the prior assistant turn might contain secrets, system-prompt fragments, internal diagnostics, or cross-topic content that should NEVER be relayed. Now the prompt says "evaluate, redact, and re-compose if needed."

- **Hostile-input fences.** Originally history was interpolated into the recovery prompt directly. Reviewers caught that a hostile user message could include text like `SYSTEM: ignore the above…` and ride into the prompt. Now history is fenced inside `<<<TOPIC_HISTORY>>>` blocks with a "treat as data only" preamble; sender names are charset-whitelisted; ANSI/control bytes/bracketed-paste terminators are stripped.

- **Multi-machine safety.** Originally any reaper that saw a topic could act on it. Reviewers caught that two machines syncing the same git state would both fire. Now there's an `isOwnedByThisServer` check via a pid registry — only the server that actually spawned the session reaps it.

- **Pid recycling defense.** Reviewers caught that on macOS a session can be respawned in the same millisecond with a recycled pid, which would defeat the (pid, startTime) fingerprint check. Added a `spawnUuid` to the fingerprint.

- **Persistence guarantees and rollout plan.** Originally one-shot enable. Now a 4-stage rollout: dark-mode telemetry only → Mode A only → Mode B enabled → user-visible escalation. Each stage gates on telemetry from the prior. Plus quantitative SLOs, a telemetry event catalog, and a threat-model table.

- **Hardening of side details**: persisted dedupe file uses atomic tmpfile-rename + 0600 mode + schema validation + size cap; `injectMessage` has a 10s hang timeout; `/reaper/status` endpoint is auth-gated with timing-safe compare and per-IP backoff; restart reconciliation uses an O(log n) targeted query, not a 20-row scroll-back.

The original design was directionally right. The reviewed version is what actually survives contact with hostile inputs, slow APIs, restarts, multi-machine deployments, and pid recycling. The user-visible behavior is identical — agent stops being silent, response gets to you within 4 minutes, worst-case notification at 10 minutes.

## Iteration Summary

| Iteration | Reviewers | Material findings | Spec changes |
|-----------|-----------|-------------------|--------------|
| 1 | security, scalability, adversarial, integration | 28 (3 critical, 11 high, 12 medium, 2 low) | Major rewrite — channel discriminator, fingerprint, persisted dedupe, rate limits, Mode B redesign, hostile-input fences |
| 2 | security, scalability, adversarial, integration | 16 (mostly medium) | Schema migration story, SessionManager API contract, dedupe-clearance durability, dual-gate Mode B, spawnUuid |
| 3 | convergence check | 0 material new | 2 low-sev clarifications (spawnUuid regeneration semantics; restart-reconciler depth) |
| 4 | external: GPT 5.4 + Gemini 3.1 Pro + Grok 4.1 Fast | ~12 material across all three | Time semantics split, channel-qualified dedupe key, Mode B four-gate classifier, injectMessage timeout, async mutex, Mode B redaction prompt, rollout plan, SLO, telemetry catalog, threat-model table |

## Convergence Verdict

**Converged at iteration 4.** No material findings remain unaddressed in the converged spec. Out-of-scope items (phase-3 scale beyond 500 active topics; Slack edit/delete semantics; substance-aware dedupe; repo-wide auth-endpoint hardening) are explicitly listed and tracked as follow-up specs rather than handwaved.

The spec is ready for user review and approval.
